forecaster_note: Small to modest peaky-to-junky surf Sat, lightest winds in the AM — waist to chest high, N corners cleanest; NE wind builds later with showers and thunderstorms around. Sun the better day: winds swing offshore as the coastal low moves away, cleaning up short-period E/NE swell for fun to good peaky surf (head high-ish), though still uncertain. Mon a possible target day. — Surfline forecaster (Fri 2 Oct)

wind.summary: Light NNE 6 kph at dawn, cross-shore N 8 kph by 9am, then NE onshore 15 kph from noon (gusts ~31), freshening to 23 kph by 6pm.

shark.summary: Northern Beaches detections in the last 24h: Manly Beach — SLS drone sighting (~17h ago); North Narrabeen — 1 tagged shark detection (~21h ago). None at Dee Why, Long Reef or Curl Curl. Feed is current (newest statewide detection 0.3h old; 69 real detections statewide in 24h). Check the live map before paddling out.

days.label: Today
days.note: Small, peaky NE wind swell (4.8ft @ 7s, ~245 kJ — fun, not powerful) plus a tiny 0.9ft S. Light NNE at dawn, cross-shore ~9am, then NE onshore from noon and freshening to 23 kph by 6pm — and showers/thunderstorms around. Mid-morning (10–12) is already onshore-ish, so go early for the lightest winds: north corners cleanest. Low 6:22am, high 1:05pm. Long Reef takes the most size.

dee-why.window: Light NNE at first light, cross-shore ~9am, onshore NE from noon. Peaky and weak into the 6:22am low — NE 55° is the good angle but it's lumpy; N corner for the cleanest peaks. Dead-S component tiny.

tip.label: North corner — frontside at the Point
tip.text: Short-period NE is the right angle at Dee Why. Frontside rights at the Point, backside lefts on the beach peaks. 7s means punchy not powerful — stay on the drive and pick the N corner.

long-reef.window: Picks up the most size of the four and rates best (fair). Lightest winds early; onshore NE builds from noon. Reef handles the minor S better than the beachies.

tip.label: Frontside rights off the reef
tip.text: Waist to chest. 7s wind swell can back off between sets — be patient and sit on the peak that lines up.

curl-curl.window: Light cross-shore early, then onshore NE. Fun and peaky when it holds shape; N end cleanest.

tip.label: Find the bank
tip.text: Waist to shoulder and peaky — look for the bank holding its shape and take the shoulder. Flowy session board.

manly.window: Smallest of the four and onshore-ish early; North Steyne is mostly an easy-one fallback.

tip.label: Sheltered fallback
tip.text: Smaller and softer. Only worth it if the others are too raw.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Winds swing offshore W (~9–10 kph till late morning) as the coastal low moves away, cleaning up a short-period E/NE swell — forecaster has fun to good peaky surf, head high to slightly above, with S corners later. Your 10am–12pm window should be clean (W ~10 kph at 10am); southerly cross-shore ~23 kph from 1pm. DAYLIGHT SAVING STARTS 2am — clocks +1h, sunrise 6:29am. Low 8:39am. Sizes estimated; forecaster flags uncertainty.

dee-why.window: Offshore W all morning — the best window of the weekend; NE swell at its ideal angle for Dee Why. Go 8–11am, low tide 8:39am. S wind from 1pm.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Sat: small, peaky NE wind swell, lightest winds early, onshore from noon with storms about — second-best day. Sun is the pick: W offshores clean up a short-period E/NE swell, fun to good head-high-ish peaks, but the forecaster says it's uncertain so recheck. Clocks go +1h at 2am Sunday. Just past the weekend: Mon 5 Oct looks like a nice-sized peaky S + E/NE mix (head high) with light morning winds — 'could be a day to target' — and Tue eases to waist–chest ENE with clean morning offshores.
